# origin compute commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `origin --help` of the release scripts/origin-cli.version pins (v3.2.0).
     Do not edit by hand: fix the help text in origincloudhq/cli, or scripts/cli_reference_overrides.yml, and rerun. -->

This page lists every `origin compute` command. For the options every `origin` command accepts, see [Global options](../../platform/reference/cli.md#global-options); for how `--project` and `--zone` default, see [Use the CLI](../../platform/access/cli.md#set-a-default-project-zone-and-region).

## origin compute

Compute service: instances, images, key pairs, volume attachments, and the instance types and image families on offer. A resource a command acts on is given by its id (`--instance`), with `--project` and `--zone`, or by its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`; `--project` and `--zone` default to the profile's `default-project` and `default-zone`. A reference, such as `--image`, `--key-pair` or a volume attachment's `--volume` (`//pvs.origincloudapis.eu/…`), takes a full name, never a relative name or an id.

Every `origin compute` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host: `https://compute.origincloudapis.eu`, or `https://compute.{region}.origincloudapis.eu` when the profile names a `region`. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). A list without `--zone` looks up the zones at the location service, not here; `ORIGINCLOUD_LOCATION_ENDPOINT` sends that lookup elsewhere. Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_COMPUTE_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-instance-type

Returns an instance type.

```sh
origin compute get-instance-type [OPTIONS] --instance-type <INSTANCE_TYPE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--instance-type <INSTANCE_TYPE>` | yes | The type to return, `instanceTypes/{instance_type}`. Its id, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`, or its relative name, `instanceTypes/{instance_type}`. |

### list-instance-types

Lists every instance type, including those no longer offered, which instances launched as them still report: check `available` before launching as one.

```sh
origin compute list-instance-types [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### get-image-family

Returns an image family.

```sh
origin compute get-image-family [OPTIONS] --image-family <IMAGE_FAMILY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--image-family <IMAGE_FAMILY>` | yes | The family to return, `imageFamilies/{image_family}`. Its id, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/{image_family}`, or its relative name, `imageFamilies/{image_family}`. |

### list-image-families

Lists every image family, including those no longer offered: check `available` before launching from one.

```sh
origin compute list-image-families [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### get-image

Returns one of the project's own images.

```sh
origin compute get-image [OPTIONS] --image <IMAGE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | yes | The image to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. |

### list-images

Lists the project's own images in a zone, oldest first. The public images are listed by `ListPublicImages`.

```sh
origin compute list-images [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone to list, such as `eu-central1-az1`. Without it, every zone that offers the service is listed, in catalog order; the profile's `default-zone` isn't used for lists. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most images to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |

### create-image

Creates an image from the project's protected snapshots in the zone. The snapshots can't be unprotected while the image exists.

```sh
origin compute create-image [OPTIONS] --description <DESCRIPTION> --root-device <ROOT_DEVICE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--description <DESCRIPTION>` | yes | What the image holds, as you describe it. |
| `--default-user <DEFAULT_USER>` | no | The account an instance launched from the image logs in as, unless the launch names another: a POSIX user name of at most 32 lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or an underscore, and not `root`. `cloud` when left empty. |
| `--root-device <ROOT_DEVICE>` | yes | The device name of the disk the image boots from: one of the `--block-device`' `device`. |
| `--block-device <KEY=VALUE,...>` | no | The image's disks, each created for an instance launched from it. One element as comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs; repeat the flag for more. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `device`, required: The slot the disk takes on every instance launched from the image: `vda` to `vdz` but `vdc`, unique within the image. It is a hint at most, not the name the guest gives the disk. In the guest, the disk's serial is its volume's id, which a Linux guest links as `/dev/disk/by-id/virtio-<volume-id>`. `size_gib`, required: The disk's size in GiB, at least the snapshot's. `source_snapshot`: The full name of the protected snapshot the disk is created from, in the image's project and zone; an empty disk when left empty. Its full name, `//pvs.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/snapshots/{snapshot}`; not a relative name or an id. A value with a comma in it goes through `--block-devices-json` too. |
| `--block-devices-json <JSON>` | no | The whole list as the API's JSON, an array of objects whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. A resource name in it is a full name, `//{service}.origincloudapis.eu/{name}`, never a relative name or an id, as in its KEY=VALUE form. Instead of `--block-device`. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's image instead of creating a second one. One is generated when not given. |

### update-image

Changes an image's description or tags.

```sh
origin compute update-image [OPTIONS] --image <IMAGE> <--description <DESCRIPTION>|--tag <KEY=VALUE>|--no-tags>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | yes | The image to change. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. |
| `--description <DESCRIPTION>` | one of `--description`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | What the image holds, as you describe it. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | one of `--description`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--description`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Remove all of its tags. |

### delete-image

Deletes an image. Instances launched from it are unaffected.

```sh
origin compute delete-image [OPTIONS] --image <IMAGE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | yes | The image to delete. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-instance

Returns an instance. A terminated instance can be read by name for a day after it was terminated.

```sh
origin compute get-instance [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |

### list-instances

Lists the instances in a zone, oldest first. A terminated instance is listed for two hours after it was terminated. For every zone's instances, list the zones whose `services` name `compute` with the location service (`location.origincloudapis.eu`), then each zone's instances.

```sh
origin compute list-instances [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone to list, such as `eu-central1-az1`. Without it, every zone that offers the service is listed, in catalog order; the profile's `default-zone` isn't used for lists. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most instances to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |

### create-instance

Launches an instance. The operation is done once the instance is `RUNNING`, or failed once it is `FAILED`, with the reason in `stateReason`; a failed instance still exists, and can be started again or deleted.

```sh
origin compute create-instance [OPTIONS] --instance-type <NAME> --key-pair <NAME> --network-interface <NAME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance-type <NAME>` | yes | The instance type by its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`, such as `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/gp1.core.2`: one whose `available` is true. Changing it needs the instance `STOPPED`. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--image <NAME>` | no | The full name of the image the boot volume is created from, in the instance's zone: one of the project's own, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`, or a public one, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. Set exactly one of `--image` and `--image-family`; launched from a family, this is the public image the family resolved to. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}` or `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--image-family <NAME>` | no | The full name of the image family to launch the current public image of, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/{image_family}`. Set exactly one of `--image` and `--image-family`. Empty when the instance was launched from an image. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/{image_family}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--key-pair <NAME>` | yes | The full name of the key pair whose public key is installed for `--login-user`, in the instance's project. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/keyPairs/{key_pair}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--login-user <LOGIN_USER>` | no | The account to log in as: a user created at first boot that holds the key pair. A POSIX user name of at most 32 lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or an underscore, and not `root`. The image's `defaultUser` when left empty. |
| `--boot-volume <KEY=VALUE,...>` | no | The boot volume: its size and storage class at launch, and the volume. The image's size on the default storage class when left out. As comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `size_gib`: The size in GiB the volume was created with, at least the image's size; the image's size when left at 0. Grow the volume itself to resize it; this keeps the size at launch. `storage_class`: The storage class by its full name, `//pvs.origincloudapis.eu/storageClasses/{storage_class}`; the default class when left empty. Its full name, `//pvs.origincloudapis.eu/storageClasses/{storage_class}`; not a relative name or an id. A value with a comma in it goes through `--boot-volume-json` too. |
| `--boot-volume-json <JSON>` | no | As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. A resource name in it is a full name, `//{service}.origincloudapis.eu/{name}`, never a relative name or an id, as in its KEY=VALUE form. Instead of `--boot-volume`. |
| `--network-interface <NAME>` | yes | The network interfaces' full names, in device order, the boot interface first; exactly one today. Each is an existing interface in the instance's project and zone that nothing else holds, created with the network service: its subnet and security groups are the instance's. Terminating the instance releases it, and it stays. An instance launched from a recipe with an interface spec, or before interfaces were named at launch, shows the interface created for it once it exists, which is deleted with the instance. Each by its full name, `//network.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/networkInterfaces/{network_interface}`; not a relative name or an id. Repeat for more. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--service-account <NAME>` | no | The full name of the service account the instance runs as, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`: a `WORKLOAD` service account of the instance's organization that isn't deleted. Launching with one, or updating the instance to one, needs `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization as well; an update that leaves it empty removes it, and a terminated instance's can't change. Empty for an instance that runs as none. Its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--local-disk <KEY=VALUE,...>` | no | Disks on the machine the instance runs on, beside its boot volume, created blank at launch; at most 16. A local disk is temporary: it comes back empty after every stop and start and after its machine restarts, and it is deleted with the instance. It can't be the boot disk, snapshotted, resized or detached, and an instance with one isn't moved to another machine while it runs. Each appears among the instance's volume attachments. One element as comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs; repeat the flag for more. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `size_gib`, required: The size in GiB, at least 1. `device`: The slot the disk takes on the instance, `vda` to `vdz` but `vdc`, and none the boot volume or another local disk has; the first free one, in the order the disks are listed, when left empty. It is a hint at most, not the name the guest gives the disk. In the guest, the disk's serial is its volume's id, which a Linux guest links as `/dev/disk/by-id/virtio-<volume-id>`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--local-disks-json` too. |
| `--local-disks-json <JSON>` | no | The whole list as the API's JSON, an array of objects whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. Instead of `--local-disk`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of launching a second instance. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### launch-instance

Launches an instance from a recipe: the instance it describes, with a network interface created from each interface spec it holds. The recipe is sent inline as `--launch-template-data`, or is a version of a launch template named by `--launch-template`, with the fields set in `--launch-template-data` overriding that version's for this launch only. Nothing is created when the launch is refused, as for an invalid field, a quota or a subnet with no address left. The operation is done once the instance is `RUNNING`, or failed once it is `FAILED`, with the reason in `stateReason`; a failed instance still exists, keeps the interfaces created for it, and can be started again or deleted.

```sh
origin compute launch-instance [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--launch-template-data <KEY=VALUE,...>` | no | The recipe of the instance to launch. Required unless `--launch-template` is set. With `--launch-template`, the fields set here override the version's for this launch only, and the version stays as it is: a field left empty keeps the version's, so an override can't clear one. `image` or `imageFamily` replaces both of the version's, `sizeGib` and `storageClass` of `bootVolume` each replace the version's own, and `tags`, `networkInterfaces` and `localDisks` replace the version's whole. As comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `instance_type`: The instance type by its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`, such as `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/gp1.core.2`: one whose `available` is true. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`; not a relative name or an id. `image`: The full name of the image the boot volume is created from, in the launch's zone: one of the project's own, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`, or a public one, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. Set exactly one of `image` and `image_family`. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`; not a relative name or an id. `image_family`: The full name of the image family to launch the current public image of, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/{image_family}`. Set exactly one of `image` and `image_family`. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/{image_family}`; not a relative name or an id. `key_pair`: The full name of the key pair whose public key is installed for `login_user`, in the launch's project. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/keyPairs/{key_pair}`; not a relative name or an id. `login_user`: The account to log in as: a user created at first boot that holds the key pair. A POSIX user name of at most 32 lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or an underscore, and not `root`. The image's `default_user` when left empty. `service_account`: The full name of the service account the instance runs as, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`: a `WORKLOAD` service account of the project's organization that isn't deleted. Launching with one needs `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization as well. Empty for an instance that runs as none. Its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`; not a relative name or an id. `boot_volume`, `tags`, `network_interfaces`, `local_disks` are set only through `--launch-template-data-json`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--launch-template-data-json` too. |
| `--launch-template-data-json <JSON>` | no | As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. A resource name in it is a full name, `//{service}.origincloudapis.eu/{name}`, never a relative name or an id, as in its KEY=VALUE form. Instead of `--launch-template-data`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of launching a second instance. One is generated when not given. |
| `--launch-template <NAME>` | no | The full name of a launch template of the instance's project to launch from, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/launchTemplates/{launch_template}` for its default version, or with `@{version}`, `@default` or `@latest` after it for that version, resolved when the launch is made. Launching from one needs `compute.launch_template.get` on it as well. An unknown template or version is refused with `NOT_FOUND`, and a version whose image, key pair or subnet is gone is refused naming that field of `--launch-template-data`. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/launchTemplates/{launch_template}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### update-instance

Changes an instance's type, tags or service account. A new `--instance-type` needs the instance `STOPPED`, and is refused with `FAILED_PRECONDITION` otherwise; it takes effect at the next start. A larger type is checked against the same vCPU quota a launch is. The operation is done once the instance shows the change.

```sh
origin compute update-instance [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE> <--instance-type <NAME>|--tag <KEY=VALUE>|--no-tags|--service-account <NAME>>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to change. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |
| `--instance-type <NAME>` | one of `--instance-type`, `--tag`, `--no-tags`, `--service-account` | The instance type by its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`, such as `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/gp1.core.2`: one whose `available` is true. Changing it needs the instance `STOPPED`. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`; not a relative name or an id. Left as it is when not given. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | one of `--instance-type`, `--tag`, `--no-tags`, `--service-account` | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--instance-type`, `--tag`, `--no-tags`, `--service-account` | Remove all of its tags. |

Launching with one, or updating the instance to one, needs `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization as well; an update that leaves it empty removes it, and a terminated instance's can't change. Empty for an instance that runs as none. Its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`; not a relative name or an id. Left as it is when not given. |

### delete-instance

Terminates an instance: its guest is stopped for good, its network interfaces are released, `AVAILABLE` again with their addresses (one created for it at launch is deleted), and its boot volume is deleted with it unless a snapshot of it exists. Other attached volumes are detached and kept. Terminating a terminated instance changes nothing. The operation is done once the instance is `TERMINATED`.

```sh
origin compute delete-instance [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to terminate. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### start-instance

Starts a `STOPPED` or `FAILED` instance. It keeps its name, its addresses and its volumes, and may come back on another machine. Starting a running instance changes nothing; it is refused while the instance is `INITIALIZING`, `STOPPING` or `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The operation is done once the instance is `RUNNING`, or failed once it is `FAILED`.


| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance to start. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |

| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### create-key-pair

Creates a key pair: imports `--public-key`, or, left empty, generates an `ssh-ed25519` key and returns its private half in `privateKey`, in this response only. A repeat of a generating request with the same `--request-id` can't return the private key again, and is refused with `CONFLICT`, its `ErrorInfo` metadata naming the key pair under `keyPair`: delete it and create another.

```sh
origin compute create-key-pair [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--public-key <PUBLIC_KEY>` | no | The OpenSSH public key line, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... comment`. Left empty, the platform generates the key pair. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows, and the comment of a generated key. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id creates no second key pair. A repeat importing a key returns the first request's key pair; a repeat generating one is refused with `CONFLICT`, as the private key went to the first request only, and the error's `ErrorInfo` metadata names the key pair under `keyPair`. One is generated when not given. |

### create-launch-template

Creates a launch template with `--launch-template-data` as its version 1, which is its default. The recipe's fields are checked for what their names say: their type, and that a key pair, a subnet, a network interface or a security group is the template's project's and a service account its organization's. Whether they exist, and are in the zone an instance is launched in, is checked at that launch.

```sh
origin compute create-launch-template [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--launch-template-data <KEY=VALUE,...>` | no | The recipe of the version this shows, `version`: the default version's unless the name named another. On creation, the recipe of version 1. As comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs. A key is a field's name, with `_` or `-`. The keys: `instance_type`, required: The instance type by its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`, such as `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/gp1.core.2`: one whose `available` is true. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/instanceTypes/{instance_type}`; not a relative name or an id. `image`: The full name of the image the boot volume is created from, in the launch's zone: one of the project's own, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`, or a public one, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`. Set exactly one of `image` and `image_family`. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/images/{image}`; not a relative name or an id. `image_family`: The full name of the image family to launch the current public image of, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/{image_family}`. Set exactly one of `image` and `image_family`. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/imageFamilies/{image_family}`; not a relative name or an id. `key_pair`, required: The full name of the key pair whose public key is installed for `login_user`, in the launch's project. Its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/keyPairs/{key_pair}`; not a relative name or an id. `login_user`: The account to log in as: a user created at first boot that holds the key pair. A POSIX user name of at most 32 lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or an underscore, and not `root`. The image's `default_user` when left empty. `service_account`: The full name of the service account the instance runs as, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`: a `WORKLOAD` service account of the project's organization that isn't deleted. Launching with one needs `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization as well. Empty for an instance that runs as none. Its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`; not a relative name or an id. `boot_volume`, `tags`, `network_interfaces`, `local_disks` are set only through `--launch-template-data-json`. A value with a comma in it goes through `--launch-template-data-json` too. |
| `--launch-template-data-json <JSON>` | no | As the API's JSON, an object whose fields are named in camel case, as the command prints them, or as the API definitions name them; `@FILE` reads it from a file. Each field and value is checked before anything is sent, at any depth. A resource name in it is a full name, `//{service}.origincloudapis.eu/{name}`, never a relative name or an id, as in its KEY=VALUE form. Instead of `--launch-template-data`. |
| `--default-version <DEFAULT_VERSION>` | no | The number of the version launches use when they name no version. 1 on creation; an update sets it to another version the template has. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own for the launch template, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. The recipe's own `--tag` are the instances'. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id creates no second launch template and returns the first request's. One is generated when not given. |

### update-launch-template

Changes a launch template's tags or its default version, or both. A version's recipe never changes.


| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | no | The instance: its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. Needed unless `--volume-attachment` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--volume-attachment <VOLUME_ATTACHMENT>` | yes | The attachment to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone` and `--instance`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}/volumeAttachments/{volume_attachment}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}/volumeAttachments/{volume_attachment}`. |

### list-volume-attachments

Lists an instance's volume attachments, the boot volume's first, then by device name. With `-` for the instance, lists every instance's in the zone, which with `--volume` finds the instance holding a volume. Detached attachments aren't listed.

```sh
origin compute list-volume-attachments [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone to list, such as `eu-central1-az1`. Without it, every zone that offers the service is listed, in catalog order; the profile's `default-zone` isn't used for lists. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance: its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most attachments to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. Either needs `--zone`. |
| `--volume <NAME>` | no | Only the attachments of this volume, by its full name; every volume's when left empty. Its full name, `//pvs.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/volumes/{volume}`; not a relative name or an id. |

### create-volume-attachment

Attaches an `AVAILABLE` volume to a `RUNNING` or `STOPPED` instance in the same project and zone. On a stopped instance the disk appears at the next start, and the operation is done at once. On a running one it is added live, and the operation is done once the guest sees it, or failed if it couldn't be added, which leaves the volume available.

```sh
origin compute create-volume-attachment [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE> --volume <NAME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | yes | The instance: its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. |
| `--volume <NAME>` | yes | The volume's full name, in the instance's project and zone. Its full name, `//pvs.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/volumes/{volume}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--device <DEVICE>` | no | The slot the volume's disk takes on the instance, `vda` to `vdz` but `vdc`; the first free one when left empty. It is a hint at most, not the name the guest gives the disk: a guest names its disks in the order it finds them, so a disk attached to a running instance often gets another name. In the guest, the disk's serial is the volume's id, which a Linux guest links as `/dev/disk/by-id/virtio-<volume-id>`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of attaching again. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### delete-volume-attachment

Detaches a volume, which then is `AVAILABLE` again. The boot volume can't be detached. On a running instance the device is removed live; if the guest doesn't release it, the operation fails and the volume stays attached. The operation is done once the volume is detached.

```sh
origin compute delete-volume-attachment [OPTIONS] --volume-attachment <VOLUME_ATTACHMENT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | no | The instance: its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}`. Needed unless `--volume-attachment` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--volume-attachment <VOLUME_ATTACHMENT>` | yes | The attachment to delete, detaching its volume. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone` and `--instance`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}/volumeAttachments/{volume_attachment}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance}/volumeAttachments/{volume_attachment}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-operation

Returns an operation as it is now. The operation is one an `origin compute` command answered with, such as the one `--no-wait` prints.

```sh
origin compute get-operation [OPTIONS] --operation <OPERATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--operation <OPERATION>` | yes | The operation. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/operations/{operation}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/operations/{operation}`. |

### wait-operation

Waits until an operation is done or `--timeout` has passed, whichever comes first, and returns it as it is then. It only reads, so a client may repeat it after a transport error. The operation is one an `origin compute` command answered with, such as the one `--no-wait` prints. Without `--timeout`, the command waits until the operation is done; Ctrl-C stops the waiting, not the operation. It prints the operation, and exits with status 1 when the operation failed, or isn't done when `--timeout` passes.

```sh
origin compute wait-operation [OPTIONS] --operation <OPERATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--operation <OPERATION>` | yes | The operation. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its full name, `//compute.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/operations/{operation}`, or its relative name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/operations/{operation}`. |
| `--timeout <DURATION>` | no | How long to wait for the operation, such as `30s` or `5m`. Without it, the command waits as long as the operation takes. When it passes first, the command prints the operation as it is and exits with status 1. |
